ticket.title: archive and unarchive resolve a key from the unified index but record the event in the root store
ticket.description:
Found 2026-11-10 when archiving every Verified ticket from the benchwork board: 262 archived, two did not.  GB-320 archived normally. MTR-17 could not, and the error named the wrong place:  Error: Ticket record at .gaugeblock/storypole/tickets/MTR-17.json: no record for MTR-17 and this event does not carry one  MTR-17 belongs to miter. handle_archive resolved the id from the store index - which at a suite root is the UNIFIED index, holding every member ticket - and then recorded the archive event through the root store, which holds no record for it. Every member ticket should have failed the same way; that only one did is why this looked like a UI quirk rather than a routing bug.  This is the same shape as GB-352 (reap), which is what made it recognisable: a root-scoped read of a suite-wide index followed by a root-scoped write.  FIX (storypole 29eb12b). archive and unarchive now ask which repository holds the key and, when it is not this one, open that store and record there, reporting it: "Archived task MTR-17 in miter". Refusing with an instruction would have been wrong for these two verbs specifically - a board archives in bulk and knows a key, not an owner - so they route instead.  repo_root_of moved into workspace::lookup so this handler and the reaper undo the dot-directory nesting once rather than twice.  Verified: MTR-17 archived in miter, and ledger-reconcile reports archived 264 with no verified bucket and no delta.

RE-CHECKED 2026-11-12: the description records the verification (MTR-17 archived in miter; ledger-reconcile reported archived 264 with no delta), and today reconcile still reports index and ledger agree with no cross-store key collisions. Closing on that.

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index f7fa257..c38f642 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 ## [Unreleased]
 
 ### Fixed
+- `storypole-core`: `event_timestamp` now reads `HandoffRecorded` from the packet's own `timestamp_ms` instead of letting it fall through to the zero arm of the timestamp table, so a handoff no longer sorts ahead of every real event. Replay by `(timestamp, id)` and replay from a legacy ledger's file order now agree, which is what `migrate` checks before it archives a ledger. Before this, any store holding a handed-off ticket that was never subsequently verified could not be migrated: `migrate` aborted with a divergence error and the written record reported the stale status (SP-54).
 - `storypole-core`: `claim` now creates and checks out the lease branch in the repository that owns the task (`scope.repo`) instead of the store root, so claiming a member task can no longer switch a harness checkout onto a feature branch; harness-level tasks record the branch without touching any checkout, and verification receipts read branch/SHA from the task's own repository (GB-137).
 
 ### Changed

         | LedgerEvent::DeferredItemCaptured { .. }
         | LedgerEvent::TaskVerified { .. }
-        | LedgerEvent::TaskClaimed { .. }
-        | LedgerEvent::HandoffRecorded { .. } => 0,
+        | LedgerEvent::TaskClaimed { .. } => 0,

index 0000000..5611a76
--- /dev/null
+++ b/crates/storypole-core/src/tickets/order_tests.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+//! Ordering against a handoff clock (`SP-54`).
+//!
+//! `HandoffRecorded` used to fall through to the `0` arm of the timestamp table, so a handoff sorted
+//! ahead of every real event no matter when it happened. A legacy ledger replays linearly, so the two
+//! orders disagreed and `migrate` refused the store; worse, the written record reported `InProgress`
+//! for a ticket that had been handed back to `ready`.
+
+#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
+
+use uuid::Uuid;
+
+use super::*;
+use crate::model::LedgerEvent;
+use gaugeblock_contracts::storypole::{HandoffPacket, TaskStatus};
+
+/// A status change at `at`.
+fn moved(id: Uuid, to: TaskStatus, at: u64) -> LedgerEvent {
+    LedgerEvent::StatusChanged {
+        task_id: id,
+        from: TaskStatus::Ready,
+        to,
+        reason: None,
+        timestamp_ms: at,
+    }
+}
+
+/// A handoff recorded at `at`, as `handoff_task` builds it.
+fn handed_off(id: Uuid, to: TaskStatus, at: u64) -> LedgerEvent {
+    LedgerEvent::HandoffRecorded {
+        task_id: id,
+        handoff: HandoffPacket {
+            recorded_by_agent: "cline".to_string(),
+            timestamp_ms: at,
+            completed_items: Vec::new(),
+            remaining_items: Vec::new(),
+            last_error_or_blocker: None,
+            git_ref: None,
+            dirty_files: Vec::new(),
+        },
+        new_status: to,
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_handoff_sorts_by_its_own_clock_not_at_zero() {
+    let id = Uuid::from_u128(4);
+    // The recorded order a real ledger holds: a claim, then a handoff 216 seconds later.
+    let mut events = vec![
+        moved(id, TaskStatus::InProgress, 200),
+        handed_off(id, TaskStatus::Ready, 260),
+    ];
+
+    order_events(&mut events);
+
+    let stamps: Vec<u64> = events.iter().map(event_timestamp).collect();
+    assert_eq!(
+        stamps,
+        vec![200, 260],
+        "the handoff carries its own clock instead of sorting at zero"
+    );
+    assert!(

task.description: Found 2026-11-10 when archiving every Verified ticket from the benchwork board: 262 archived, two did not.  GB-320 archived normally. MTR-17 could not, and the error named the wrong place:  Error: Ticket record at .gaugeblock/storypole/tickets/MTR-17.json: no record for MTR-17 and this event does not carry one  MTR-17 belongs to miter. handle_archive resolved the id from the store index - which at a suite root is the UNIFIED index, holding every member ticket - and then recorded the archive event through the root store, which holds no record for it. @@ -9,6 +9,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 ## [Unreleased]
 
 ### Fixed
+- `storypole-core`: `event_timestamp` now reads `HandoffRecorded` from the packet's own `timestamp_ms` instead of letting it fall through to the zero arm of the timestamp table, so a handoff no longer sorts ahead of every real event. Replay by `(timestamp, id)` and replay from a legacy ledger's file order now agree, which is what `migrate` checks before it archives a ledger. Before this, any store holding a handed-off ticket that was never subsequently verified could not be migrated: `migrate` aborted with a divergence error and the written record reported the stale status (SP-54).
 - `storypole-core`: `claim` now creates and checks out the lease branch in the repository that owns the task (`scope.repo`) instead of the store root, so claiming a member task can no longer switch a harness checkout onto a feature branch; harness-level tasks record the branch without touching any checkout, and verification receipts read branch/SHA from the task's own repository (GB-137).

+//! Ordering against a handoff clock (`SP-54`).
+//!
+//! `HandoffRecorded` used to fall through to the `0` arm of the timestamp table, so a handoff sorted
+//! ahead of every real event no matter when it happened. A legacy ledger replays linearly, so the two
+//! orders disagreed and `migrate` refused the store; worse, the written record reported `InProgress`
+//! for a ticket that had been handed back to `ready`.
+
+#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
+
+use uuid::Uuid;
+

+/// A status change at `at`.
+fn moved(id: Uuid, to: TaskStatus, at: u64) -> LedgerEvent {
+    LedgerEvent::StatusChanged {
+        task_id: id,
+        from: TaskStatus::Ready,
+        to,
+        reason: None,
+        timestamp_ms: at,
+    }
+}
+
+/// A handoff recorded at `at`, as `handoff_task` builds it.
+fn handed_off(id: Uuid, to: TaskStatus, at: u64) -> LedgerEvent {
+    LedgerEvent::HandoffRecorded {
+        task_id: id,
+        handoff: HandoffPacket {
+            recorded_by_agent: "cline".to_string(),
+            timestamp_ms: at,
+            completed_items: Vec::new(),
+            remaining_items: Vec::new(),
+            last_error_or_blocker: None,
+            git_ref: None,
+            dirty_files: Vec::new(),
+        },
+        new_status: to,
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn a_handoff_sorts_by_its_own_clock_not_at_zero() {
+    let id = Uuid::from_u128(4);
+    // The recorded order a real ledger holds: a claim, then a handoff 216 seconds later.
+    let mut events = vec![
+        moved(id, TaskStatus::InProgress, 200),
+        handed_off(id, TaskStatus::Ready, 260),
+    ];
+
+    order_events(&mut events);
+
+    let stamps: Vec<u64> = events.iter().map(event_timestamp).collect();
+    assert_eq!(
+        stamps,
+        vec![200, 260],
+        "the handoff carries its own clock instead of sorting at zero"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        matches!(events.last(), Some(LedgerEvent::HandoffRecorded { .. })),
+        "replay ends on the handoff, so a handed-off ticket reads ready"
+    );
+}
